## How they got there
Arsenal finished as runners-up after losing the final to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties. Their campaign was defined by a dominant league phase profile, where they achieved a perfect 3.0 points per game and a 2.38 goal difference per game, beating 100% of teams in those categories during the season. They also excelled defensively with just 2.8 opponent shots on target per game, outperforming 97% of their league phase opponents.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would have selected Arsenal as a top contender, ranking them second among all knockout teams and placing them inside its top two predictions. With a calculated probability of 24.6% to reach the final, they outperformed the base rate of 8.3% for a random team. The model's expectation aligns closest with reaching the semi-finals on its scale. This high ranking was driven primarily by a positive SHAP contribution of 0.78 from their goal difference per game, while their attacks per game contributed -0.16 to the prediction.

## Weak spots
Arsenal committed fouls at a rate that placed them below only 11% of teams in the league phase. Their long passing volume was lower than 36% of their peers during the same period. Additionally, they averaged fewer passes per game than 39% of the teams they faced in the league phase.

SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Use 'significant' or 'significantly' only for a Holm-adjusted p-value comparison, never for other differences. Write plain markdown without tables.
